solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Significant wit to hold spades

indicators.note: a word that holds something keeps it inside itself, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a wit is a funny person, a comic
S is the card-suit abbreviation for spades

explanation.surface: A notable comedian manages to keep hold of some spades, perhaps at a card table.
explanation.walkthrough: The comic holds S between his second and third letters: CO-S-MIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, cosmic describes something vast or of great importance, so it can stand for significant.

clue.text: Face up to hot refreshment

indicators.note: hot here means agitated or excited, so the letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Confront a steaming drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Face up to' reads as an idiom meaning confront, and 'hot' as a description of the drink; the three words are the fodder and hot is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A cup of tea is the classic British refreshment, an example of a drink offered to revive someone.

clue.text: Latest lie reproduced — it goes round at the highest levels

definitions.text: it goes round at the highest levels

indicators.note: something reproduced is made again, here in a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The newest falsehood is repeated everywhere, even in the top circles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goes round at the highest levels' sounds like gossip among the elite; it is literally an object orbiting high above the Earth.
explanation.definitionFit: A satellite orbits a planet high in space, so it goes round at the highest altitude.

clue.text: Greek character in radio talkathon

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: the letters straddle the two words

explanation.surface: A Greek personality appears on a long radio chat show.
explanation.definitionFit: Iota is the ninth letter of the Greek alphabet, and a character is a letter.

clue.text: Punish meet returning into hunt

indicators.note: into says one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: to hunt is to chase

indicators.note: something returning comes back the way it went, so the word is read from end to start

parts.note: a committee or court that meets is said to sit

explanation.surface: A huntsman wants a hunt meet that keeps coming back to be disciplined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Meet' looks like the gathering of a hunt, which suits the surface, but here it is the verb: a body that meets sits.
explanation.definitionFit: To chastise is to rebuke or discipline someone severely, a direct synonym of punish.

clue.text: One going against the flow at this point cut short credit

indicators.note: cutting something short trims its end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: here means at this point
buying on tick is buying on credit

explanation.surface: A rebel at this stage has had their credit curtailed.
explanation.walkthrough: To buy on tick is British slang for buying on credit.
explanation.definitionFit: A heretic holds views opposed to accepted doctrine, someone going against the prevailing current.

clue.text: Put on trainer? One that used to be held up

definitions.text: One that used to be held up

parts.note: to put on a play is to stage it
a trainer is a coach

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether to put on a training shoe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trainer' looks like a shoe; 'held up' means robbed by highwaymen, not supported.
explanation.definitionFit: Horse-drawn stagecoaches were the classic targets of highway robbers in centuries past.

clue.text: One is on all but tender feet

indicators.note: all but means everything except the final letter

parts.note: one is becomes I am, with I for one
to tender is to make a bid

explanation.surface: Someone is stuck on sore feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tender feet' reads as sore feet, but tender is an offer and feet are units of verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Iambi, the plural of iambus, are metrical feet of one short and one long syllable.

clue.text: Think highly of upcoming encounters with European

indicators.note: in a down answer, coming up means read from the bottom, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: encounters are meetings, so meets
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: Admire forthcoming meetings with a European.
explanation.definitionFit: To esteem someone is to respect and admire them, so it is thinking highly of them.

clue.text: Sullen TV detective snatching what looks like a doughnut

indicators.note: snatching something means grabbing it and holding it within

parts.note: Inspector Morse is the Oxford detective of British TV
the letter O is ring-shaped like a doughnut

explanation.surface: A glum television detective grabs a doughnut.
explanation.definitionFit: Morose means gloomy and ill-tempered, a close synonym of sullen.

clue.text: Indulged Italian female with our small sweet cake

parts.note: to pet is to indulge or pamper
IT is the abbreviation for Italian
F is the abbreviation for female
taken as written

explanation.surface: A spoilt Italian woman shares our little cake.
explanation.definitionFit: A petit four is a small fancy cake or biscuit served with coffee, so a small sweet cake describes it.

clue.text: Allow Mike to appear in opening

indicators.note: appearing in something means standing inside it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: an adit is a horizontal entrance into a mine, an opening
Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone lets Mike make his entrance at an opening night.
explanation.walkthrough: An adit is a mine entrance, a crossword favourite for opening.
explanation.definitionFit: To admit someone is to let them in, so it matches allow as a verb of permission.

clue.text: Cut down area of pasture

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to bring down a tree or a person
second meaning: a stretch of upland moor in northern England used for grazing

explanation.walkthrough: In northern England a fell is a hill or high moorland where sheep graze.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for chopping down trees and a noun for upland grazing ground.

clue.text: What dart players do is conform

definitions.meaning: first meaning: literally put a foot to the throwing mark, the oche
second meaning: an idiom for obeying the rules

explanation.walkthrough: Darts players must stand with their toes at the oche, the line on the floor they throw from.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to obey rules or accept authority, which is what conforming is.

clue.text: Mother, for example, blocking boy's diet

indicators.note: blocking means standing around and closing in, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: a mother is an example of a parent
a boy's name

explanation.surface: A mother stops her son's eating regime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mother' tempts as the definition, since Westminster is the mother of parliaments; the definition is diet, a legislative assembly as in Japan.
explanation.definitionFit: A diet is a formal legislative assembly, as in Japan or historically Germany, so it is a parliament.

clue.text: Move abroad, good to go for Abu Dhabi, say

indicators.note: the abbreviation for good is told to go away, leaving the rest

parts.note: to move abroad to live is to emigrate
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Relocating overseas, with the green light given, to Abu Dhabi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Good to go' reads as a phrase meaning ready, but it splits: G is to go from the word for move abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Abu Dhabi is one of the seven emirates of the UAE, so it is an example, hence 'say'.

clue.text: Pick cold pipe with nothing inside

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

indicators.note: with followed by inside says the next piece has something placed within it
inside says the round letter goes within the pipe word

parts.note: a hose is a flexible pipe
nothing is zero, shaped like O

explanation.surface: Select a cold, empty pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: To pick is to select from options, which is what choose means.

clue.text: Great like the '60s full of energy

indicators.note: full of says one piece contains the other

parts.note: the 1960s were the Swinging Sixties
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Something brilliant, just like the lively decade of the 1960s.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1960s in Britain were dubbed the Swinging Sixties.
explanation.definitionFit: Swingeing means very large or severe, as in swingeing cuts, so it can mean great in size.

clue.text: Daughter with resolution knowing horse discipline

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter
RES is the abbreviation for resolution
sage means wise, knowing

explanation.surface: A determined, wise daughter takes up a riding event.
explanation.walkthrough: RES is short for resolution, as in screen resolution.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressage is the equestrian sport of training a horse to perform precise movements.

clue.text: Being on the ball become teary

definitions.meaning: second meaning: tears rising in the eyes

explanation.walkthrough: As an adjective phrase the answer means knowledgeable; as a verb it means tears are gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone well up in a topic is on the ball about it, and eyes that well up fill with tears.

clue.text: Fit to drink with staff clutching ticket

indicators.note: clutching means gripping tight, so one piece holds the other within

parts.note: a staff is a pole
a tab is a label or ticket

explanation.surface: Bar staff grip the ticket for a drinkable order.
explanation.definitionFit: Potable water is safe for drinking, so potable means fit to drink.

clue.text: I plonked into chair being comparatively rough

indicators.note: plonked into means dumped inside, so the letter goes within the other piece

parts.note: a rocker is a rocking chair
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone drops heavily into a chair that turns out to be rather uncomfortable.
explanation.definitionFit: Rocky describes rough, uneven ground, so its comparative means rougher.

clue.text: Resist pulling up Romeo over time

indicators.note: in a down answer, over means placed above the next piece
pulling a word up a down light reads it from the bottom, so it runs backwards

parts.note: a Romeo is a lover
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A girl resists dragging her Romeo away when time's up.
explanation.walkthrough: Romeo is not R from the phonetic alphabet here but a lover.
explanation.definitionFit: To revolt is to rise up against authority, so it means to resist.

clue.text: Hysterically spare about piano rags

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go around the extra one
something done hysterically is wild and disordered, so the letters are thrown around

parts.note: taken as written
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: Someone goes wild about old cloths around the piano.
explanation.walkthrough: Rag is slang for a low-quality newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Rags are disparaging slang for newspapers, which are papers.

clue.text: Striking area I have found east of a forest finally

indicators.note: in an across answer, east of means placed to the right, so these pieces come after

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word before it

parts.note: the last letter of forest
a tract is an area of land
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: A notable area I have discovered east of the end of some woodland.
explanation.definitionFit: Striking looks are good-looking and eye-catching, a synonym of attractive.

clue.text: From the beginning the tie is a metaphor

indicators.note: from the beginning points to the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: the first letter of the
a rope is used to tie, a tie

explanation.surface: The necktie has always stood for something more.
explanation.definitionFit: A trope is a figure of speech, and a metaphor is a classic example of one.

clue.text: Reports must dispel trouble for a long time

indicators.note: dispelling something drives it away, so those letters are removed

parts.note: reports passed on are messages
to be in a mess is to be in trouble

explanation.surface: News reports have to get rid of worries for good.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove MESS from the start of MESSAGES and AGES is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, ages means a very long time, as in 'I waited for ages'.

clue.text: Produce permit

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to give birth or yield fruit

explanation.walkthrough: Both words read as nouns, farm goods and a licence, but each is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear children or fruit is to produce them, and to bear something is to put up with or allow it.

clue.text: Degrade poem on old monarch

indicators.note: on means next to, so the poem follows on from the monarch

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen
an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: A poem about a former king or queen that wears them down.
explanation.definitionFit: To erode is to wear away gradually, which is to degrade or weaken something.

clue.text: Dancing arena with bill for me?

definitions.text: Dancing arena with bill for me?

indicators.note: dancing letters move about and settle in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dancer asks whether that theatre with her name on the playbill is for her.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is a riddle spoken by the performer: an arena where she is on the bill, dancing, is hers.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballerina is a female ballet dancer, the one who would top the bill in a dancing arena.

clue.text: Paste we spread round English bloomer

indicators.note: round says the rearranged letters go around the extra letter
spreading something out rearranges it, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: We smear paste around an English loaf.
explanation.walkthrough: A bloomer is a British crusty loaf, which suits the paste; here it is a thing that blooms, a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet pea is a scented garden flower, and a bloomer is a crossword-only sense for a flowering plant.

clue.text: Second-rate scoundrel's accent

parts.note: B grade is second-rate
a rogue is a scoundrel

explanation.surface: A low-grade villain has a distinctive way of speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: A brogue is a regional accent, especially an Irish or Scottish lilt.
